chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad from Hariz from Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan said:

A group of our companions performed Hajj, and when they arrived in Medina, they entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: 'Zurarah ordered us to recite the Talbiyah with a loud voice (Nahl) when we entered into Ihram.' He said to them: 'Perform Tamattu'.' When they left from his presence, I entered upon him and said to him: 'May I be your ransom, by Allah, if you do not inform them of what you informed Zurarah of, they will surely go to Kufa and become known as liars there.' He said: 'Send them back to me,' so they entered upon him, and he said: 'Zurarah is truthful.' Then he said: 'By Allah, no one will hear this from me after today.'

key_terms.أُحرِمنا: We entered into the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah).
key_terms.الكوفة: Kufa, a major city in Iraq and a center of Shia scholarship.
key_terms.تَمَتّعُوا: Perform Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj).
key_terms.زُرَارَة: Zurarah ibn A'yan, a prominent companion and scholar known for transmitting fiqh rulings.
key_terms.كذّابا: Liars / those known for falsehood (here implying they would be questioned or deemed unreliable if they changed their practice without clear authority).
key_terms.نُهِلّ: We recite loudly / with a loud voice (from the root N-H-L, implying raising the voice).

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the loud recitation of the Talbiyah during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the scholarly nuance between the permissibility of performing Tamattu' Hajj and the specific juristic preference (or ruling) regarding the audibility of the Talbiyah, as transmitted by Zurarah. The Imam’s declaration that 'no one will hear this from me after today' is interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating a transition to a more permanent or definitive stance on the matter, or perhaps the cessation of this specific transmission chain, underscoring the dynamic nature of fiqh derivation in the early Imami tradition.
